title: Pandya Dynasty
capsule: The window 592-922 covers the first Pandyan empire, the dynasty's early-medieval revival centered on Madurai in the far south of the Tamil country. Kadungon (r. c. 560-590), recorded in the Velvikudi inscription as the destroyer of the Kalabhras, restored Pandya rule south of the Kaveri; his successors Maravarman Avanisulamani and Arikesari Maravarman contested the Pallavas through the seventh century. The empire peaked under Jatila Parantaka Nedunjadaiyan (Varagunavarman I, c. 765-815), who annexed the Kongu and Venadu countries, and Srimara Srivallabha (c. 815-862), who raided Sri Lanka and sacked Anuradhapura before being checked by the Pallavas. The rise of the Cholas ended this first empire: Varagunavarman II was crushed near Kumbakonam around 880, and Chola Parantaka I captured Madurai about 910, subordinating the Pandyas and closing this period of independence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Pandya core territory around Madurai is well attested from inscriptions; the full extent of their dominion during the 13th-century expansion is less precisely mapped.
